title: Reverse the handing of a mortise lock's latchbolt so the jamb's strike latches on it
instruction: Reverse the handing of the latchbolt on the mortise lock in the holder, so that the jamb ends closed and held latched by its strike, with the grippers off the lock and the jamb.
context: Done by: general maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00; 1,529,700 US workers, BLS OEWS 2025) and locksmiths (49-9094.00), who install and repair door hardware. A mortise lock ships for one door hand; fitted to a door of the other hand, the bevel faces away from the strike and the latch cannot catch, so the door is left unsecured: closing it, the strike lip meets the latch's square back and the door will not latch. The maker's installation instructions give the field change: pull out the latch and rotate it 180 degrees; the case stays closed and no tool is needed.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Lock case, fixed: grade-1 commercial mortise lock case, 11.3 x 15.4 x 2.5 cm, standing on its back edge in a padded bench holder (8 x 19 cm base, two 4.5 cm cheeks) at (32.0, -15.0), long axis along y, faceplate up with its top 12.8 cm above the bench. Armored front: 3.2 x 20.3 cm stainless steel with a 1.75 x 2.95 cm latchbolt opening at its centre. Latchbolt: brass with a satin chrome finish, 1.6 x 2.8 cm head, beveled on the +x side, standing out 1.9 cm (full throw), spring-returned; it can be pulled out 1.3 cm further, turns only when its tail clears the opening, and can be pushed in flush. Jamb: an oak jamb section (7 x 26 x 2.5 cm) with a 12.4 x 3.2 cm stainless strike, face down 0.3 cm above the faceplate, on a linear guide along x at y = +2.0 (its far end); it starts open, 9 cm toward -x, and a light spring (about 1 N) returns it there. Closing it (+x) brings the strike lip onto the latchbolt's -x face; at its stop the strike opening sits over the latchbolt. A 3 x 5 x 2 cm push block stands on its -x end over the guide. Visual-only bench props, no collision, lying flat: end-cutting pliers and a claw hammer.
scoring: Measured at the end of the run with a protractor, a ruler and a photo; nothing earlier in the run counts. 1.0: the latchbolt's bevel faces -x (turned 180 +- 10 degrees from the start), the jamb is within 0.3 cm of its stop and the latchbolt stands 1.9 +- 0.1 cm out into the strike opening (latched), and both grippers are off: each gripper's tool-centre point is outside a box made of the faceplate and the jamb over its whole travel (x 19.4 to 35.4, y -25.2 to +3.5), grown by 5 cm on every side, from the bench up to 22.6 cm above it (5 cm above the push block). The run ends as a success once this has held for 1 s. 0.7: bevel reversed and latched as for 1.0, but a gripper's tool-centre point is inside that box. 0.4: bevel reversed, but not latched (jamb open, sprung back or short of its stop, or the latchbolt held in). 0: bevel not reversed (untouched, pulled and let go, left turned 90 degrees, turned back), whatever the jamb does: with the square back toward the strike, the jamb stops on the lip 4.2 cm short and springs back. Possible: 0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0.
reset_notes: Open the jamb (pull it back to its -x end), pull the latchbolt out, turn it back so the bevel faces +x, and let it seat at full throw.
fidelity: Case, front, throw and strike outline 1:1 from the makers' dimensions; head size, 6.5 mm key engagement, 0.2 N/mm latch spring, strike opening and lip, and the jamb's 1 N return spring are estimated (not published). A linear guide replaces the door's swing over its last 9 cm at the latch (nearly straight there). Case and holder are fixed. The handing screw (locking functions only) is out of scope.
